 Navajo Stirling says Jiri Prochazka 'gets hit a lot,' expects easy work
 Sourav Chakraborty Nov 18, 2026 
 Navajo
Stirling believes Jiri
Prochazka ’s defensive openings could give him a path to victory
in the 
UFC Qatar main event on Nov. 21.
The unbeaten New Zealander plans to stay technical against the
former 
Ultimate Fighting Championship light heavyweight ace, whose
willingness to absorb strikes he hopes to exploit.
 Advertisement 
 Unbeaten Navajo Stirling plans to exploit Jiri Prochazka's
striking defense in UFC Qatar main event
“I think the principle remains the same. Like, he gets hit a lot,”
Stirling told UFC News. “I think he's got one of the highest
significant strikes absorbed per minute above the UFC light
heavyweight average, and I'm going to look to capitalize on that
and hit him square and just keep it technical and just try and find
the chin.”
“So yeah, it should be easy work,” he said.
Despite his confidence, Stirling said he wasn’t looking beyond
Prochazka.
“Not really, not so much. I think for me, the way it's all playing
out, just taking it little by little, so I haven't really thought
too much. Ahead. I don't really want to. I'm just thinking about
this fight, you know, because none of this, all that happens until
you gotta win with the fight right in front of you,” he added.
Stirling is coming off a first-round stoppage of former UFC light
heavyweight champion Jan
Blachowicz in August. Beating Prochazka would give him a second
consecutive win over a former champion.
 "Hit him square, keep it technical, try to
find the chin. Should be easy work." Navajo Stirling
(@navajostirling) has a clear game plan for his first main event at
